**Park Ji‑sung** (박지성) is a retired South Korean professional footballer who played primarily as a midfielder. He was born on **May 25, 1981** in Seoul, South Korea.

### Career Highlights

| Period | Club | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| 1999–2000 | **Pohang Steelers** (K League) | Started his professional career in South Korea. |
| 2000–2005 | **VfB Stuttgart** (Bundesliga, Germany) | First major move to Europe; helped the club win the Bundesliga in 2006. |
| 2005–2012 | **Manchester United** (Premier League, England) | Joined on a free transfer. Became a fan favourite for his work‑rate, stamina, and versatility. Won the Premier League (2007–08, 2008–09), FA Cup (2008–09), and the UEFA Champions League (2007–08). |
| 2012–2013 | **FC Seoul** (K League) | Returned to South Korea to finish his playing career. |

### International Career

- Represented the **South Korea national team** from 2000 to 2014.
- Earned **108 caps** and scored **12 goals**.
- Key tournaments: 2002 FIFA World Cup (co-hosted by South Korea), 2006, 2010, and 2014 World Cups; 2004, 2007, 2011, 2015 AFC Asian Cups.
- Known for his leadership and consistency; served as captain for many matches.

### Playing Style

- Renowned for his **endurance**, **tactical intelligence**, and **versatility**—capable of playing both defensive and attacking midfield roles.
- Nicknamed “The Iron Man” for his ability to cover large areas of the pitch and maintain high performance throughout matches.

### Post‑Retirement

- After retiring in 2013, Park has been involved in various football-related activities, including coaching roles, punditry, and ambassadorial duties for football development in South Korea.

### Legacy

Park Ji‑sung is widely regarded as one of South Korea’s greatest footballers and a pioneer for Korean players in European leagues. His dedication, professionalism, and achievements have left a lasting impact on the sport both domestically and internationally.
